content.title: About
content.content: Candy Mint (5111) are small mint-flavored candies coated with a sugary glaze. They offer a refreshing mint taste combined with a sweet note, making them a popular treat after meals and as a breath freshener.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Candy Mint first appeared in the early 20th century in Europe as a breath‑freshening confection.
The sugary glaze helps preserve the mint aroma longer.
The recipe often includes natural menthol, which intensifies the cooling sensation.
These candies are frequently used in film and theater as a prop for “minty” scenes.
In some countries they are sold in small packets of 10–20 pieces.

items.title: Freshens breath
items.content: Menthol and mint stimulate saliva production, neutralizing unpleasant mouth odors.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Mint can help ease mild gastrointestinal discomfort.

items.title: Reduces fatigue
items.content: The menthol aroma provides a mild stimulating effect, increasing alertness.

items.title: Menthol allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to menthol or flavoring agents.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption can contribute to tooth decay and raise blood glucose levels.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Large amounts of mint candies may cause heartburn in people with high gastric acidity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Candy Mint is best enjoyed one at a time, allowing the menthol to gradually release its aroma. They can be taken after a meal, as a small snack, or added to dessert presentations for a minty accent.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the candies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. Properly stored, they retain flavor and aroma for up to 12 months.
